1.why: The submitted token's SHA-256 hash is compared against session.resetTokenHash stored on the requesting session, so the code is verified as belonging to that user/session.

2.why: The token hash is stored per-session, so any other session has no matching resetTokenHash and the same code is rejected as invalid.

3.why: /api/set-password only mutates the current session and contains no logic to invalidate other existing sessions, so prior sessions remain usable until their 30-minute expiry.

4.why: The server refuses to start without TLS certificates and sets HSTS, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned and relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as Argon2id hashes — hashing rather than encryption, but appropriate algorithms for the data.

6.why: The simulated delivery message is generic and carries only the recovery code, disclosing no account existence or other private user data.

7.why: Email, token, and password inputs are validated with strict allow-list regexes, JSON parsing is content-type and size restricted, and all dynamic text is written via textContent.

8.why: Navigation uses only local location.hash routes, no outgoing URL is ever followed, and the prefilled code from the hash is regex-validated.

9.why: Simulated messages are plain strings rendered exclusively with textContent and contain no HTML or script derived from user input.

10.why: The recovery token and MFA code are returned in the API response (testToken/testMfaCode) and written to the on-page 'Logs' panel and browser console.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed and tokens hashed at rest, but the MFA code '246810' is hardcoded in plaintext and the initial password literal appears in the source.

12.why: There is no login endpoint and the initial password is marked not usable, yet the hardcoded universal MFA code '246810' effectively functions as a default credential.

13.why: A rate limit of 5 attempts per 60 seconds returns 429, but it is enforced per-session and can be bypassed by starting a new session.

14.why: The reset endpoint always returns the same generic message ('If an eligible account exists...') regardless of whether the email is registered.

15.why: The token is 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues (base64url, ~43 chars), stored only as a hash, single-use, short-lived, and bound to the requesting session.
